summary: This is a legitimate fix-forward addendum on the still-open PR #610 (branch worker/task-20260727-193351-sales-pipeline-interactive-dashboard--co), addressing the three gaps a prior audit flagged: RLS was missing on the new org-scoped compliance.crm_sales_targets table, the table was unregistered in the asset-registry-coverage guardrail, and setSalesTarget lacked finite-number input validation. I checked out the actual PR branch tip in a worktree (not just the pasted diff) and independently confirmed: the new migration 0268 adds ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus app_runtime_tenant_isolation/service_role_bypass policies and org_id/(org_id,month) indexes that match the established pattern in drizzle/0101 exactly, and that src/lib/db/tenant-scoped.ts's real withTenantContext implementation genuinely runs app_runtime queries with no RLS bypass, so the claimed DB-level isolation is real, not aspirational. The asset-registry and terminology-guardrail-exemptions.yaml edits are properly justified with dated reasons consistent with this repo's existing entries, and Number.isFinite(targetValue) validation was added to setSalesTarget as claimed. I re-ran `bun x tsc --noEmit` myself on the checked-out branch and it came back clean, confirming that part of the self-report; `bun test` and `bun x eslint` produced no output/exit 1 in this review sandbox (looks like a sandbox restriction on those specific commands, not a real tool failure) so I could not independently re-execute the test suite, but I read every new/changed test file directly and the assertions are logically sound against the real implementation they exercise. Two minor, non-blocking issues are worth a human's attention before merge (noted below) but neither is a security hole or a reason to reject.
issues: src/lib/services/crm-service.ts's setSalesTarget uses a find-then-insert/update pattern with no DB-level UNIQUE constraint on (org_id, month) on compliance.crm_sales_targets -- two concurrent POSTs for the same org+month could race and create two target rows for that month instead of one being an update; low severity (admin-only input, not attacker-reachable data corruption) but worth a follow-up UNIQUE(org_id, month) constraint.

src/lib/services/sales-pipeline-rls.test.ts asserts via regex against the migration file's own SQL text, i.e. it can catch someone later deleting/editing the RLS clause but cannot catch a live-Postgres behavioral bug (e.g. a wrong function name) since there's no live DB connection available in this sandbox -- the test's own header is honest about this limitation, flagging only so the human reviewer doesn't mistake it for a live RLS verification.

Could not independently re-run `bun test` / `bun x eslint` in this review environment (both returned exit 1 with zero output, looks like a sandbox restriction rather than a real failure) to reconfirm the self-reported 32/32 tests passing and clean lint -- tsc was independently reverified clean; recommend the human merger spot-check `bun test` output before merging if that assurance matters.
